findings.summary: the new T1 case's third assertion (refusedForAnotherPod().isZero()) is true by FIXTURE construction, not by the meter's logic -- no mutation of the refusal scan can red it
findings.detail: The fixture is Faults.none() with podb un-partitioned, so the release window injects NOTHING: `during` is empty and `refusedForAnotherPod` is 0 for every mutant of the scan loop. MEASURED in a throwaway worktree of the staged index, full :sequencer:test, 495 tests: hoisting `refusedForAnotherPod++` ABOVE the own-pod carve-out (the exact over-count mutation this file's other comments name as the live threat) reds CommitProtocolSweepTest.theInvariantsHoldAcrossEverySeed, GracefulReleaseMeterTest.TWORefusalsInOneWindowAreCountedTWICE and GracefulReleaseMeterTest.theLEADERSOWNPartitionIsSEENButBlamedOnNOBODYElse -- and leaves THIS assertion green. No coverage is lost (three siblings carry it), and the test's verdict rests on lines 68-74, which are measured-sensitive. The finding is that the `.as` text -- 'the refusal direction saw nothing, which is why this counter had to exist' -- reads as evidence that the two counters are independent UNDER MUTATION, when it is true by construction of the fixture. That is the same family that killed M5.26's first meter (a comparison true by construction in a single-threaded driver, which both reviewers named). review.md rule 11: record, do not fix.
findings.failure_scenario: A future hand tightens the refusal scan in GracefulReleaseMeter (M5.28/M5.30's open thread), over-counts refusedForAnotherPod, opens GracefulReleaseMeterTest to check the direct pins, and reads `refusedForAnotherPod()).isZero()` at line 75 with 'the refusal direction saw nothing' beside it -- concluding the two counters are pinned as independent under mutation. MEASURED they are not: hoisting `refusedForAnotherPod++` above the own-pod carve-out reds the sweep and two siblings and leaves this line GREEN, because the fixture injects no fault so `during` is empty for every mutant of the scan.

findings.summary: M5.51's disposition is honest and its key claim is measured-correct, but two of its stated facts are wrong: the untyped run is FOUR ints (six counting the two ahead of it), not three, and the release components are read by ONE test, not by 'the protocol tests'
findings.detail: The deferral itself is not an evasion and I re-measured the claim it rests on: replacing `releases.releasedDespiteOwnPartition()` with `releases.refusedForAnotherPod()` at CommitProtocolSimulation.java:625 leaves ALL 495 sequencer tests green including the 1,000-seed sweep, and both counters are honestly 0 on a correct tree, so no numeric relation over the sweep's totals can separate them (unlike M5.28's case, which had 38 against 1,608). Nor can any INPUT separate them: `observe` sets the actor to the leader, so `releasedDespiteOwnPartition` is 0 for every input `run` accepts, and `run`'s only injection seam takes a reader view. Rung 1 is the right answer and a minor is correctly deferred. Two corrections for whoever picks the row up. (1) 'THE THREE ADJACENT ints' is stale: Result now ends `int gracefulReleases, int gracefulReleasesRefusedForAnotherPod, int gracefulReleaseRefusalsSeen, int gracefulReleasesDespiteOwnPartition` -- four from one object, preceded by `int readersChecked, int midRunDrained`, so the compile-clean transposition surface is six. CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:460 carries the same 'three adjacent `int` components' sentence, pre-existing and made an undercount by this commit. (2) 'A Result component is read by CommitProtocolSweepTest and by the protocol tests, so this is a mechanical but multi-file change' overstates the blast radius of the fix it proposes: `grep -rln gracefulRelease sequencer/src` returns three files -- CommitProtocolSimulation (the producer), CommitProtocolSweepTest (four accumulator lines) and GracefulReleaseMeterTest (which reads the METER, not the Result). The protocol tests read OTHER Result components and would not be touched. Failure scenario: the row is sized as a large multi-file change and deferred a second time, when it is a ~3-file, ~15-line rung-1 edit.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever picks up M5.51 reads 'THREE ADJACENT ints' and 'read by CommitProtocolSweepTest and by the protocol tests', sizes it as a large multi-file refactor, and defers it a second time -- while the actual rung-1 edit is ~3 files and ~15 lines (Result signature, one construction site, four accumulator lines in the sweep). Worse, the stale count leaves the `int readersChecked, int midRunDrained` pair ahead of the group unnamed, so a record that wraps only the four release counters is taken to have closed the whole untyped run when two compile-clean transposable ints remain beside it.
